- `src/audit/audit-service.mjs:47-50`, `src/audit/audit-query.mjs:41,49-51`, `src/platform/listing.mjs:1`: The actor summary counts only the first `limit` matches. `actorSummary` passes the prepared query, including `limit`, to `summarizeActors`, which calls `selectEntries`. `selectEntries` uses `pageOf(...)`, and `pageOf` slices to `page.limit` before the counts are built. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:146` requires "counts every entry it matches, ignoring `limit`". With more matching entries than `limit` (default 500), the reported `entries` counts are truncated. Fix: build the actor counts from the full filtered set using the same match predicate, without applying the `limit` slice.
- `src/badges/badge-service.mjs:5-7,15-17`, `src/platform/append-log.mjs:6-8`: The badge event key lookup is limited to the submitted event's building. `findKeyedEvent` calls `store.list(event)`, and `createAppendLog` filters `list` by `buildingId` when it is supplied. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:167` requires "if an event recorded in any building has the key, recording returns it and does no further work." A retry of an event key recorded in building A, submitted for building B, is therefore recorded again as a new event. Fix: perform the key lookup over all recorded events (no building filter) before the repeated-swipe check and append.
- `src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:12`: The credit reason is stored trimmed instead of exactly as supplied. `prepareCredit` returns `reason: credit.reason.trim()`. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:135` requires "its `reason` must not be blank after trimming; the reason is stored exactly as supplied." Given a supplied reason `"  Loyalty  "`, the stored credit becomes `"Loyalty"`, and the invoice carries the altered text. Fix: keep the validation on the trimmed value, but store `credit.reason` unchanged.
- `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7`: Only the first inner double quote is doubled. `quoteField` uses `text.replace(/"/, '""')`, which has no `g` flag. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:241` requires "with inner double quotes doubled". For the value `a"b"c`, the output is `"a""b"c"`, where the second quote is not doubled, so the CSV field is malformed. Fix: use `text.replace(/"/g, '""')`.
- `src/exports/value-format.mjs:29`: List items are formula-prefixed, although the spec says they are written as stored. `formatList` maps each item through `formatText`, which prefixes `'` to items starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:243` states "a `list` of strings is joined with `;`, its items written as stored", and only `text` values receive the `'` prefix at `governing-spec.md:242`. A room amenity `=pool` is exported as `'=pool` instead of `=pool`. Fix: join the list items without applying `formatText`, while keeping the string-type check.
- `src/members/allowance.mjs:12`: Reservations that start exactly at the start of the usage month are excluded from used minutes. `countedReservations` tests `overlaps(instant(reservation.startAt), period)`, and `overlaps` requires `right.startAt < left.endAt` (`period.startAt < startAt`) for a zero-length instant. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:154` requires "the total length in minutes of the member's `confirmed` reservations whose `startAt` is within the month", and `governing-spec.md:150` defines the usage month as half-open. A confirmed reservation starting at `Date.UTC(year, month - 1, 1)` is therefore not counted in `used`, `remaining`, `overage` or `reservationIds`. Fix: test `period.startAt <= reservation.startAt && reservation.startAt < period.endAt` directly, instead of using `overlaps` with an instant.
- `src/messaging/messaging-service.mjs:53-56`: The outside-quiet-hours message is sent before its save is awaited. The code calls `const saved = store.save(sent);`, then `await send(sentNotice(sent));`, then returns `saved`. The store write is queued on a promise chain and completes later, so `send` receives `{messageId, memberId, body}` before the message is saved as `sent`. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:207` requires "saved as `sent` with `sentAt` from `now()` before `send` receives `{messageId, memberId, body}`". A failed save would also still have sent the notice. Fix: `const saved = await store.save(sent); await send(sentNotice(saved)); return saved;`.
- `src/messaging/quiet-hours.mjs:35`: The release time is one minute late when `now()` is not on a minute boundary. `releaseTime` computes `minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1) + minutes(wait)`, where `wait` is measured from the local minute of `at` (the floor), but the base is the ceiling of `at`, which is one minute later. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:206` requires `releaseAt` "at the first minute boundary after `now()` whose local minute is `endMinute`". Reproduced with an isolated copy of the staged files: `now()` at 10:00:30 local with `endMinute` 602 returns a release at local minute 603 (10:03), 150000 ms after `now()`, instead of 10:02 (90000 ms after `now()`). Fix: compute the release from the floor of `at`, for example `minuteStart(at) + minutes(wait)`, which is strictly after `at` because `wait` is at least 1 whenever the message is quiet.
- `src/reservations/transitions.mjs:16-17`, `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:37,45,58`: Transitions modify the reservation object they receive. `applyTransition` builds `next` with `{...record, state: rule.to}`, which shares the `history` array with `record`, and then calls `next.history.push({state: rule.to, at})`. `confirmReservation`, `cancelReservation` and `rescheduleReservation` therefore append to the caller's `history`. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:8` requires "Operations never modify a reservation object they receive; they return new records." Example: after `confirmReservation(reservation, ...)`, the caller's `reservation.history` contains a `confirmed` entry while `reservation.state` is still `held`. Fix: copy the history array (`history: [...record.history, {state: rule.to, at}]`) before appending.
- `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:53-66`: Rescheduling does not enforce the duration limit on the snapped window. `rescheduleReservation` snaps the window and checks availability, but never calls `exceedsMaxDuration(window)`, although `createReservation` does at line 14. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:197` requires "the snapped window must satisfy the duration limit and be available." A reschedule to a window longer than 240 minutes is saved as a `held` reservation of that length. Fix: reject with a "too long" error when `exceedsMaxDuration(window)` is true, before the availability check.
- `src/reservations/catalog.mjs:16`: Amenity matching is wrong when a room lists the same amenity more than once. `hasAmenities` returns `new Set([...room.amenities, ...amenities]).size === room.amenities.length`, which compares the distinct count with the raw array length. For `room.amenities` `["wifi", "wifi"]` and no requested amenities, the result is false, so `listEligibleRooms` excludes the room and `createReservation` rejects it, even though `governing-spec.md:77` requires only that "a room must contain every requested amenity" (vacuously true here). For a request of `["wifi"]`, the room is also rejected. Fix: test membership directly, for example `amenities.every((amenity) => room.amenities.includes(amenity))`.
- `src/schedules/closures.mjs:26` (used at `src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs:31,56`): `hasEnded` truncates the remaining time to whole minutes, so a closure that has not ended can be treated as ended. `hasEnded` is `minutesBetween(at, closure.endAt) <= 0`, and `minutesBetween` is `Math.trunc((to - from) / MINUTE)`. A closure whose `endAt` is 30000 ms after `now()` yields `trunc(0.5) = 0`, so `addClosure` rejects it as "already ended", and `upcomingClosures` omits it. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:184` rejects a closure "whose `endAt` is not later than `now()`", and `governing-spec.md:189` lists upcoming closures as those whose `endAt` is "later than `now()`". Fix: compare the instants directly, `closure.endAt <= at`.
- `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7,9-10`: A report room entry without an `active` field is treated as active. `ENTRY_DEFAULTS` sets `active: true`, and `prepareRoom` spreads it under the supplied entry, so an absent `active` becomes `true`. `loadDirectory` then selects it. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:149` selects only "rooms whose `active` value is `true`", and `governing-spec.md:75` states "Only rooms whose `active` value is `true` may be booked or listed." An absent value is not `true`. Example: `{id: 'r1', buildingId: 'b1', capacity: 4}` is included in the utilization report although it has no `active` value. Fix: remove the `active: true` default, so only an explicit `true` selects the room (the reservation catalog's `isActiveRoom` already uses this strict rule).
- `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:58-64` (with `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:242`): An expired offer can be accepted. `acceptOffer` calls `moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at)` and then checks `isLapsing(next, at)`, but `next.state` is already `accepted`, so `isLapsing` is always false. The `accept` rule (`entry-states.mjs:242`) also has no expiry check. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:50` requires "Only a nonexpired `offered` entry may be accepted", and `governing-spec.md:182` defines an offer as expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`. Example: an offer with `expiresAt` 15 minutes before `at` is accepted and set to `accepted`. Fix: check `isLiveOffer(entry, at)` on the entry before the transition, or add an expiry check to the `accept` action.
- `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:244`: The 60-minute withdrawal limit applies to `waiting` entries. The rule `{action: 'withdraw', from: ['waiting', 'offered'], ..., cutoff: WITHDRAW_CUTOFF_MINUTES}` rejects any withdrawal with `entry.startAt - at < 60` minutes, whether the entry is `waiting` or `offered`. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:183` states: "Withdrawing an `offered` waitlist entry is rejected when its `startAt` is less than 60 minutes after `now()`. A `waiting` entry has no such limit." Example: a `waiting` entry starting in 30 minutes cannot be withdrawn. Fix: give the cutoff only to the `offered` source state, and move `waiting` into a separate rule with no cutoff.
- `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:8-10,13` (with `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:14`): Late-invoice fees are never charged. `intentRequest` returns `{requestKey, invoiceId, memberId, total}` and drops `issuedAt`. `createPaymentIntent` passes that object to `newIntent`, which computes `lateFee(prepared.total, prepared.issuedAt, at)`. With `issuedAt` undefined, `dueAt` is `NaN`, so `isLate` is false and `fee` is 0. Governing spec `governing-spec.md:267` requires "An intent created while its invoice is late has a `fee` of 5 percent of `total`, rounded down to a whole unit". Example: an invoice with `issuedAt` 20161 minutes before `now()` and `total` 1000 gets `fee` 0 and `amount` 1000 instead of `fee` 50 and `amount` 1050. Fix: carry `issuedAt` through `intentRequest` (and into `newIntent`'s input).
